cover-01.bio2:

Full stack polyglot development consultant with passion for creating IoT, mobile, web, and cloud products with a flair for user experience and user interface design.
cover-01.notes:
This talk came about because I (Bob) broke production.

At a conference I (Bob) saw a reported error and tried to diagnose it in our Cloudflare Super Script.

I (He) found the issue and clicked Deploy on the way out the door.

30ms later, things started to fail and this talk was born.

hackathon-intro.title: Hackathons: Introduction
hackathon-intro.text1:
Common hackathon constraints ...
  • Very short timelines.
  • Limited infrastructure resources.
  • Need for quick iteration and fast demos.
hackathon-intro.text2:
Personal Implementations ...
  • Tried Angular (took too long to initialize and pull down).
  • Used HTML, CSS, & jQuery-lite (have experience with jQuery).
  • Had others generate mock data (excel converted to JSON).
Thoughts ...
  • Implementing features without framework can't scale past event.
  • No "real" functionality (Create, Read, Update, & Delete).

why-are-we-here.title: We Are Here ...
why-are-we-here.text2:
Cloudflare
  • Worker Scripts
  • Key Vaults
  • D1 Database
Super Script: Built a tool for managing ...
  • Redirects
  • Split-tests
  • Dynamic Content
This script handles millions of Worker Script hits per day.
why-are-we-here.notes:
• For our client, we had to build tooling to allow for consolidation of redirects, split tests, and content transformation based on path and URL parameters.
  • The decision to use Cloudflare made for us; it was the right decision.
  • These captures show 3M requests (average is 4M) at an average of 36ms!

overview.title: Overview
overview.text1:
1. Accounts (with Users)
  2. Domains
  3. Pricing
  4. Worker Scripts (APIs, CRON Jobs, Environment Variables, Secrets)
  5. Key Vaults (fast document database)
  6. D1 Database (SQLite)
  7. Pages (repository or upload; frameworks)
  8. Image Storage (transformations)
overview.notes: We're going to take a look at several parts of what Cloudflare can do. Remember, I switched to HTML, CSS, and jQuery because there was minimal setup and configuration. The same can be said for Cloudflare.

01-02--accounts-domains.title: Accounts & Domains
01-02--accounts-domains.text1:
Accounts
  • Manage > Members allows invitation of members.
01-02--accounts-domains.notes: Create a new account for the event. Add your main account and anyone else you feel is needed for the event.

03--pricing.title: Pricing
03--pricing.text1:
Pricing (Workers plans: Free)
  • Worker & Pages Functions (10ms CPU, 100k/day)
  • Builds (1 concurrent slot)
  • D1 (100k writes/day, 5GB)
  • KV (100k read/day, 1k write, delete, list/day)
  • Hyperdrive (100k queries/day)
03--pricing.text2:
Pricing (Workers plans: Paid)
  • Worker & Pages Functions (15min CPU, 10M/day)
  • Builds (6 concurrent slots)
  • D1
  • KV
  • Hyperdrive (unlimited)
03--pricing.notes: While looking at these differences in Free versus Paid, you have to remember that this is for a Hackathon. But, it is only $5.00 per month.

04--worker-script-notes.title: Worker Scripts
04--worker-script-notes.text1:
Think "API." ...
  • JavaScript
  • TypeScript
  • Python
  • Rust
Findings ...
  • 60-second cache.
  • Connect: Routes, DB, KV, Secrets (and more).
  • Free 100,000 requests/day (paid, no limit).
  • Module Pattern (import/export, multiple files).
  • ctx.waitUntil (extend lifetime of worker).
  • Cron Jobs.
04--worker-script-notes.text2:
Keep in mind ...
  • Cache-buster, CORS, paging.
Deployment
  • GitHub Actions (build process).
  • Connect to Github via Settings (was able to not build).
Options
  • Sites deployed as Worker Scripts rather than Pages (this feature is the direction Cloudflare is going and will develop code for; Pages will have limited improvements in the future).
04--worker-script-notes.notes: This is not a Node.js Server, a Lambda, or a Function App. It's a very small script that runs as a man-in-the-middle, taking the request and allowing for manipulation or replacement of the content. It can access Key Vaults and Databases as well.

05--key-vault-notes.title: Key Vaults
05--key-vault-notes.text1:
Findings ...
  • Low Latency, Edge Compute.
  • 1,200 rw/5-minutes (have to rethink large number of writes).
Data ...
  • key (512B)
  • value (5MB)
  • metadata (1kB)
05--key-vault-notes.text2:
Keep in mind ...
  • Metadata: can only see via API.
  • This is where it's easy to hit the paywall limit.

06--database-d1-notes.title: D1 Databases
06--database-d1-notes.text1:
D1 is Cloudflare's managed, serverless database with SQLite's SQL semantics, built-in disaster recovery, and Worker and HTTP API access.

Findings ...
  • 500 MB (free), 10GB (paid)
  • 100 Columns/Table, Unlimited Rows

Findings ...

07--pages.title: Pages
07--pages.text1:
Findings ...
  • Available on all plans.
  • Unlimited bandwidth (Free)
  • 500 deploys per month (Free)
  • Cloudflare is recommending Pages in favor of Workers.
07--pages.text2:
Findings (deprecation) ...
  • Workers are low-latency and at the edge.
  • Existing projects, use Pages. New projects, use workers.

cloudflare-summary-and-best-practices.title: Cloudflare Summary & Best Practices
cloudflare-summary-and-best-practices.text1:
Summary
  • Cannot be client-side application.
  • Manipulate DOM Elements.
  • Add Cookies.
  • Reroute/Redirect (301 & 302 Status Codes).
  • API: keep in mind cache-buster, CORS, paging.
  • Access to Domain, Path, and Parameters.
  • GitHub Actions (build process) VERSUS Github via Settings (was able to not build).
cloudflare-summary-and-best-practices.text2:
Best Practices
  • DEV Environment: Ensure it has paid access.
  • Watch KV Read/Write Limits (use bulk where possible).
  • Build processes add code (impacts run time).
  • Cache-bust the 60-second cache.
  • Use the module pattern (import/export)
  • Use the extended worker lifetime (ctx.waitUntil)

hackathon-summary-and-best-practices.title: Hackathon Summary & Best Practices
hackathon-summary-and-best-practices.text1:
Summary
  • Start from templates/boilerplates; save time.
  • Keep Cloudflare organized; name Workers clearly.
  • Use environment variables for API keys.
  • Use the free tier limits wisely (KV limits, Worker request limits).
  • Monitor limits using the Analytics tab.
